wtb.name: Thierry Henry
award: PFA Players' Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: Arsenal's all-time record goalscorer and the focal point of the Invincibles side that went unbeaten through the 2003–04 Premier League season.

wtb.name: Gheorghe Hagi
award: UEFA Jubilee Golden Player of Romania
wtb.blurb: Nicknamed 'the Maradona of the Carpathians', he is widely considered Romania's greatest player and lifted the UEFA Cup with Galatasaray in 2000.

wtb.name: Zinedine Zidane
wtb.blurb: Scored twice in the 1998 World Cup final and hit one of the great Champions League final goals, a left-foot volley for Real Madrid in 2002.

wtb.name: Jay-Jay Okocha
award: Africa Cup of Nations Best Player
wtb.blurb: Famed for outrageous dribbling, the Bolton and PSG playmaker inspired the terrace chant 'so good they named him twice'.

wtb.name: David Beckham
award: BBC Sports Personality of the Year
wtb.blurb: Won league titles in England, Spain, the United States and France, in a career that also included loan spells at Preston and AC Milan.

wtb.name: Roger Milla
wtb.blurb: At 38, his corner-flag celebrations made him the story of Italia 90, as Cameroon became the first African nation to reach a World Cup quarter-final.

wtb.name: Hristo Stoichkov
wtb.blurb: A key part of Johan Cruyff's Barcelona 'Dream Team' and the only Bulgarian to win the Ballon d'Or.

wtb.name: Georgi Kinkladze
award: Manchester City Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: A mesmerising dribbler who lit up Maine Road in the mid-90s. City fans still rank him among the most gifted players in the club's history.

wtb.name: Ronaldinho
wtb.blurb: Won the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and is remembered as one of the most joyful, skilful players of his generation.

wtb.name: Cesc Fàbregas
award: PFA Young Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: Left Barcelona's academy for Arsenal at 16, captained the club, then went home to the Camp Nou before winning two titles at Chelsea.

wtb.name: Andriy Shevchenko
wtb.blurb: Scored the winning penalty in the 2003 Champions League final and later became Ukraine's head coach.

wtb.name: Diego Maradona
wtb.blurb: Captained Argentina to the 1986 World Cup, scoring both the 'Hand of God' and the 'Goal of the Century' against England in the same match.

wtb.name: Kevin Keegan
wtb.blurb: Two-time European Footballer of the Year who later managed Newcastle's 'Entertainers' and England.

wtb.name: David Ginola
award: PFA Players' Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: Swept both the PFA and FWA player of the year awards in 1999, the season he helped Tottenham win the League Cup.

wtb.name: Ruud Gullit
wtb.blurb: Dreadlocked captain of the Netherlands' Euro 88 winners who later became the first overseas manager to win the FA Cup.

wtb.name: Peter Schmeichel
wtb.blurb: Captained Manchester United to the Champions League in his final game for the club, completing the 1999 Treble.

wtb.name: Gianfranco Zola
wtb.blurb: Scored the Cup Winners' Cup final winner seconds after coming on as a substitute, and was later voted Chelsea's greatest ever player.

wtb.name: Dennis Bergkamp
award: PFA Players' Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: Arsenal's 'non-flying Dutchman', remembered for his touch, his vision and a famous spin-and-finish goal at Newcastle in 2002.

wtb.name: Ian Rush
wtb.blurb: Liverpool's all-time record goalscorer, with 346 goals across two spells at the club.

wtb.name: Fernando Torres
wtb.blurb: Scored the winner in the Euro 2008 final and once cost Chelsea a then-British record fee of £50 million.

wtb.name: Patrick Vieira
wtb.blurb: Born in Senegal, he became the driving force of Arsène Wenger's Arsenal and won the World Cup and the European Championship with France.

wtb.name: Luís Figo
wtb.blurb: His move from Barcelona straight to Real Madrid in 2000 made him the most hated man at the Camp Nou.

wtb.name: Pavel Nedvěd
wtb.blurb: Long blond hair, endless running and a ferocious shot with either foot. He stayed with Juventus when they were sent down to Serie B.

wtb.name: Alan Shearer
award: PFA Players' Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: The Premier League's record scorer with 260 goals, and Newcastle's all-time top scorer.

wtb.name: Gary Lineker
wtb.blurb: Never booked or sent off in his whole career, and now the long-serving face of Match of the Day.

wtb.name: Mesut Özil
wtb.blurb: Arsenal's record signing in 2013 and the king of the assist, with 19 in one Premier League season.

wtb.name: Ruud van Nistelrooy
award: PFA Players' Player of the Year
wtb.blurb: A penalty-box predator who scored 150 goals for Manchester United and later managed PSV.

wtb.name: Ian Wright
wtb.blurb: Signed by Crystal Palace from non-league aged 21, he went on to become Arsenal's record scorer until Thierry Henry passed him.

mix.name: Wayne Rooney
mix.blurb: Manchester United's record goalscorer, and England's too until Harry Kane passed him in 2023.
hints: Born in Croxteth, Liverpool.
Aged 16, he scored a late winner for Everton that ended Arsenal's 30-match unbeaten run.

mix.name: Luka Modric
mix.blurb: Won the 2018 Ballon d'Or after leading Croatia to the World Cup final.
hints: Born near Zadar, Croatia. His family became refugees during the war.
Had early loan spells at Zrinjski Mostar and Inter Zaprešić.

mix.name: Lionel Messi
mix.blurb: Eight Ballon d'Ors, and a World Cup winner with Argentina in 2022.
hints: Born in Rosario, Argentina.
Joined Barcelona's La Masia academy at 13, with the club paying for his growth hormone treatment.

mix.name: Didier Drogba
mix.blurb: Scored the late equaliser and the winning penalty as Chelsea won the 2012 Champions League final.
hints: Born in Abidjan, Ivory Coast, and moved to France aged five to live with his footballer uncle.
Signed his first professional contract at Le Mans.

mix.name: Erling Haaland
mix.blurb: Set the Premier League record of 36 goals in a season in his first campaign with Manchester City.
hints: Born in Leeds while his father played for Leeds United.
Scored nine goals in one match for Norway at the 2019 Under-20 World Cup.

mix.name: Paolo Maldini
mix.blurb: Spent all 25 seasons of his career at AC Milan and won five European Cups.
hints: Born in Milan, the son of former AC Milan captain Cesare Maldini.
Made his Serie A debut aged 16.

mix.name: Mohamed Salah
mix.blurb: Liverpool's Egyptian King and a two-time African Footballer of the Year.
hints: Born in the village of Nagrig, Egypt.
Started his senior career at El Mokawloon (Arab Contractors) in Cairo.

mix.name: Andres Iniesta
mix.blurb: Scored the extra-time winner for Spain in the 2010 World Cup final.
hints: Born in the small village of Fuentealbilla, Spain.
Joined Barcelona's La Masia academy aged 12.

mix.name: Gareth Bale
mix.blurb: Wales's record goalscorer, with an overhead kick in the 2018 Champions League final.
hints: Born in Cardiff, Wales.
Came through Southampton's academy at the same time as Theo Walcott.

mix.name: Thomas Muller
mix.blurb: A 2014 World Cup winner and Bayern Munich's record appearance maker.
hints: Born in Weilheim, Bavaria.
Spent his whole European career at Bayern Munich before joining Vancouver Whitecaps in 2025.

mix.name: Steven Gerrard
mix.blurb: Captained Liverpool's comeback from 3–0 down to win the 2005 Champions League final in Istanbul.
hints: Born in Whiston, Merseyside.
Joined Liverpool's academy at nine years old.

mix.name: Eden Hazard
mix.blurb: PFA Players' Player of the Year in 2015, and a two-time Premier League winner with Chelsea.
hints: Born in La Louvière, Belgium.
Played for Royal Stade Brainois as a boy before joining Lille.

mix.name: Kylian Mbappe
mix.blurb: A World Cup winner at 19, and scorer of a hat-trick in the 2022 final.
hints: Grew up in Bondy, a suburb of Paris.
Made his Ligue 1 debut for Monaco aged 16.

mix.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
mix.blurb: Five Ballon d'Ors, and the all-time top scorer in men's international football.
hints: Born in Funchal, on the Portuguese island of Madeira.
Played for Madeira clubs Andorinha and Nacional as a boy before Sporting CP.

mix.name: Robin van Persie
mix.blurb: Won the Premier League Golden Boot in back-to-back seasons, first with Arsenal and then with Manchester United.
hints: Born in Rotterdam.
Scored a famous flying header against Spain at the 2014 World Cup.

mix.name: Peter Crouch
mix.blurb: Scored 108 Premier League goals, a record 53 of them with his head, and became famous for his robot dance.
hints: Played for Tottenham, Liverpool, Stoke and seven other English clubs.
Scored 22 goals in 42 games for England.

mix.name: Kevin De Bruyne
mix.blurb: Belgian playmaker who won six Premier League titles with Manchester City.
hints: Born in Drongen, near Ghent, Belgium.
Chelsea sold him to Wolfsburg in 2014; City signed him the following year.

mix.name: Zlatan Ibrahimovic
mix.blurb: Won league titles in the Netherlands, Italy, Spain and France, and is Sweden's all-time top scorer.
hints: Born in Malmö, Sweden.
Scored a 30-yard overhead kick against England in 2012.

mix.name: Jamie Carragher
mix.blurb: Played 737 games for Liverpool, a total beaten only by Ian Callaghan.
hints: Born in Bootle, Merseyside.
Spent his whole professional career at Liverpool and won the Champions League in 2005.

mix.name: Michael Owen
mix.blurb: Won the 2001 Ballon d'Or, the year he scored a hat-trick in England's 5–1 win in Germany.
hints: Born in Chester.
Burst onto the world stage aged 18 with a solo goal against Argentina at the 1998 World Cup.

mix.name: Virgil van Dijk
mix.blurb: Became the world's most expensive defender when Liverpool signed him from Southampton in January 2018.
hints: Born in Breda, Netherlands.
Came through Willem II's academy, then played for Groningen and Celtic.

mix.name: Ian Wright
mix.blurb: Late starter who became one of Arsenal's greatest strikers and a well-known TV pundit.
hints: Joined Crystal Palace from non-league football aged 21.
Scored 185 goals for Arsenal.

mix.name: Harry Kane
mix.blurb: England's record goalscorer, who moved from Tottenham to Bayern Munich in 2023.
hints: Won the World Cup Golden Boot in 2018.
Spurs' all-time top scorer with 280 goals.

mix.name: Rio Ferdinand
mix.blurb: Elegant centre-back who won six Premier League titles and the 2008 Champions League with Manchester United.
hints: Came through the youth ranks at West Ham.
Leeds sold him to Manchester United for a British record fee in 2002.

mix.name: John Barnes
mix.blurb: Jamaican-born winger who won two league titles with Liverpool and scored a famous solo goal for England in Brazil.
hints: Started at Watford under Graham Taylor.
Rapped on England's 1990 World Cup song 'World in Motion'.

mix.name: Paul Scholes
mix.blurb: Ginger-haired Manchester United midfielder with 11 Premier League titles, admired for his passing and long-range goals.
hints: Spent his entire career at Manchester United.
Came out of retirement in 2012 to play on for another 18 months.

mix.name: David Seaman
mix.blurb: Arsenal and England goalkeeper famous for his moustache and ponytail.
hints: Won 75 England caps.
Won three league titles with Arsenal, the first in 1990–91.

mix.name: Ashley Cole
mix.blurb: Left-back with 107 England caps, a record seven FA Cups and the 2012 Champions League with Chelsea.
hints: A member of Arsenal's unbeaten Invincibles in 2003–04.
Crossed London from Arsenal to Chelsea in 2006.
